concepts.name: The SVD Connection
concepts.summary: Any update matrix factors as delta-W = U*Sigma*V^T (SVD); singular values sigma measure per-direction importance and, for fine-tuning updates, DECAY FAST. Keeping the top r (Eckart-Young: the optimal rank-r approximation) and grouping B = U_r*Sigma_r, A = V_r^T gives exactly LoRA's B*A shape. The key refinement: LoRA never forms delta-W nor runs an SVD; it directly LEARNS a rank-r factorization B*A by gradient descent to minimise the task loss (not to reconstruct a given delta-W). SVD is the THEORY explaining why low rank suffices, not a pipeline step.

concepts.name: Effective Rank
concepts.summary: The effective rank of an update is the number of dominant singular directions before the elbow where the singular-value spectrum collapses toward zero. It sets how large r must be: fast-decaying sigmas (steep cliff) mean a tiny subspace and a tiny r suffices; slow decay (a broad, flat spectrum) means the change is spread across many directions and r must grow. Not a pre-computed formula but the shape of the spectrum the useful update would have.
